methodologyNotes: Covers self-balancing two-wheel personal transporters sold at a published US price, marketed and retailed as 'hoverboards' — classic flat twin-platform boards, big-wheel off-road variants, and knee-control-bar 'self-balancing scooters' (the Segway-Ninebot S-series), which US retailers file under the same hoverboard category. Three seeds were corrected against verified current product lines: 'Hover-1 Titan Pro' does not exist as a distinct SKU — the actual current product is 'Hover-1 Titan'; 'Halo Rover X2' does not exist — the actual current product is 'Halo Rover X'; 'Tomoloo Q3' has no verifiable current spec sheet or retail listing — the actual currently-documented and sold variant is 'Tomoloo Q3-C' (confirmed via the manufacturer's own made-in-china.com and Alibaba storefronts), so the entry was corrected to that SKU. max_speed_kmh and range_km hold the manufacturer's stated maximum figures, converted from the published mph/mi to km (rounded to 1 decimal); where a manufacturer publishes the value directly in km/h or km it is used as-is. Independent lab/real-world test results (ERideHero, TechGearLab) frequently come in lower than the manufacturer's marketing claim — those tested figures are never substituted into the spec columns, only noted in each product's provenance for context. motor_power_w is the manufacturer's stated total motor wattage (both hub motors combined, e.g. 'dual 250W' -> 500); a few manufacturers (Segway-Ninebot) publish a combined peak/rated power figure rather than a simple per-motor continuous rating, flagged in provenance where relevant. max_load_kg is the manufacturer's maximum rider weight, converted from lbs (or used directly where a manufacturer states kg). wheel_size_in is the nominal wheel/tire diameter in inches. battery_wh is the pack capacity in watt-hours, computed from the manufacturer's published voltage x amp-hours when Wh is not stated directly; null when neither figure is published. ip_rating is the manufacturer's stated ingress-protection code (e.g. 'IPX4', 'IP54', 'IP56'); null when unpublished. ul2272_certified is true when the manufacturer states compliance with UL 2272 (the US electrical/fire safety standard for self-balancing boards) or its newer bifurcated UL 2271 (battery) / UL 2272 (vehicle) pairing. app_control is true when a manufacturer states a companion smartphone app for settings/telemetry/firmware, false when a source explicitly confirms no app exists (or only a Bluetooth speaker, no app, is offered), and null when unpublished or genuinely ambiguous. priceUsd prefers the manufacturer's own list/MSRP figure over a temporary sale price; where only a retailer price was verifiable, that figure is used and flagged. Six DTC brand storefronts (gotrax.com, swagtron.com, epikgo.com, hover-1.com, ridejetson.com, haloboard.com, all Shopify-hosted) returned HTTP 429 to every fetch attempt made during this compilation — reproduced independently via a direct curl request and via a real headless-Chromium browsing session, not a one-off tool fluke, and confirmed as a Cloudflare-level block (visible in response headers) rather than a per-page issue. For those brands, spec and price figures are corroborated instead through at least one independently-fetched retailer, reseller, or lab-test page (Newegg, Wellbots, Gearscoot, ePoweredMotion, Bikes4Sale, TechGearLab, ERideHero) plus the manufacturer's own published text as it appears verbatim in that independent source; no figure in this file was invented, and several fields (e.g. Hover-1 Titan and Swagtron T6 Outlaw prices, Tomoloo Q3-C's US retail price, EPIKGO Sport's top speed) are left null because no accessible source stated them. All images were downloaded and visually inspected before inclusion to confirm they depict the exact named product.

products.name: Segway Ninebot S2
products.priceNote: ePoweredMotion (authorized Segway reseller) lists the Ninebot S2 at $649.00. Segway's own US store (segway.com) geo-redirected to a French storefront and returned 404 for this SKU under automated access during compilation, so its price text could not be independently confirmed; Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, and Tractor Supply all list the identical SKU but did not expose price text to any fetch attempt.
products.provenance: ePoweredMotion's product page (source), fetched directly, states: 11.2 MPH top speed, 21.7 mile range, 1600W motor, 220 lb weight capacity, 10.5-inch off-road tubeless pneumatic tires, 335 Wh battery (4.5 hr charge), UL-2272 certification, IP54 waterproof rating, 'Smart APP Management', and a $649.00 price. Segway's own product page at segway.com/self-balancing/products/ninebot-s2.html (corroboration) is the canonical listing referenced by Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, Tractor Supply, and Segway's own regional storefronts (segway.la, aicmotorsports.com) for this exact SKU — Segway/Amazon copy independently confirms the 11.2 mph / 21.7 mi / 335 Wh / 4.5 hr-charge / UL-2272 figures verbatim, but the page geo-redirected to a French locale and 404'd under every automated fetch attempt during this compilation, and the Amazon/Walmart/Best Buy listings for the same SKU returned bot-check pages or stripped price text, so the $649 price rests on the reseller citation alone. The 1600W figure is a manufacturer-stated combined/peak motor rating, not a simple per-hub-motor continuous wattage — flagged because Segway's higher-tier S-MAX states a notably higher 4800W under the same reseller's spec-block convention, consistent with S-MAX being the higher-performance sibling rather than a data error.

products.name: Segway Ninebot S-MAX
products.priceNote: ePoweredMotion (authorized Segway reseller) lists the Ninebot S-MAX at $649.00 — identical to the S2 listing from the same reseller, which is a caveat worth flagging (see provenance). Segway's own US/regional store pages could not be fetched directly during compilation.
products.provenance: ePoweredMotion's product page (source), fetched directly, states: 12.4 MPH top speed, 23.6 mile range, 4800W motor power, 220 lb weight capacity, 10.5-inch wheels, 432 Wh battery, and UL-2272 certification (TUV Rheinland). Segway's own regional pages (ninebot.com US path, ap-en.segway.com, segway.la — corroboration and general research) independently describe the S-MAX as the 'supercharged' sibling of the base Ninebot S with two hub motors, an air-cooled 432 Wh battery, 4 hr fast-charge, a retractable knee-steer bar with Leansteer technology, and Segway-Ninebot App control for lights/lock/battery/firmware — all consistent with the reseller figures, though those pages separately state an 88-187 lb (40-85 kg) rider range rather than a single 220 lb max, a discrepancy left unresolved (99.8 kg / 220 lb used here as the simpler, more common 'max load' framing). Segway's own storefronts returned 404/geo-redirect/429 responses to every direct fetch attempt during compilation, so the $649 price and IP rating (not stated anywhere found) rest on the single reseller citation and are flagged accordingly — notably, the same reseller lists the base S2 at an identical $649, which is a real limitation of this price source rather than confirmation that S2 and S-MAX share a list price.

The battery's 25V figure (as published by Wellbots) is unusually low for a 36V-class hoverboard platform and was not independently corroborated, so battery_wh is left null rather than computed from a figure of uncertain reliability.

products.name: Razor Hovertrax 2.0
products.priceNote: $349.99 MSRP, quoted verbatim on Razor's own product page (razor.com/product/hovertrax-20/).
products.provenance: Razor's own product page (source), fetched directly, states: 8 mph max speed, 'up to 40 mins' battery life (a time figure, not a distance — Razor does not publish a mile/km range for this model, so range_km is left null rather than estimated), 135W cruising / 350W peak dual hub motors (350W peak used as motor_power_w), a 176 lb recommended max rider weight, a 36V lithium-ion quick-change battery pack (no Ah/Wh stated), and 'electrical system certified compliant with UL2272'; the page names Razor as 'the first US brand to receive the UL 2272 listing for safety'. It does not mention Bluetooth, an app, wheel size, or an IP rating, so those are recorded as false/null rather than assumed present. TechGearLab's independent lab review (corroboration), fetched directly, tested a notably higher 8.9 mph top speed and only a 3.4 mi range on smooth pavement (69 min runtime on an obstacle course), and cites a 220 lb weight limit rather than Razor's own 176 lb recommendation — both discrepancies are real and left unresolved, with the manufacturer's own recommended-weight and speed figures retained in the spec columns per this file's methodology. Razor's press release (PR Newswire, 'Razor Introduces a Radical New Way to Ride with Hovertrax 2.0') dates the launch to 2016.
